function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limits page | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | TxDOT – Mobile Phone Use | | **Alcohol & Driving** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is DUI.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green = go; yellow = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop.
• Yield signs give right‑of‑way to vehicles already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.001–545.020 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have right‑of‑way at crosswalks. | TxDOT – Right‑of‑Way Rules | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep left lane for passing; stay in right lane unless passing.
• Do not change lanes without signaling. | Texas Transportation Code §545.015 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | TxDOT – Parking Rules | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus. | Texas Transportation Code §545.015 | | **Vehicle Inspection & Registration** | • Annual vehicle inspection required for most vehicles.
• Registration renewal is due annually; penalties for late renewal. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) – Vehicle Inspection | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | TxDMV – Insurance | | **Special Situations** | • **Towing**: Must use a tow bar or chain; cannot tow a vehicle that is not in motion.
• **Emergency Vehicles**: Must yield to police, ambulance, and fire trucks. | Texas Transportation Code §545.015 | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT**: Regularly publishes updates on road conditions, speed limits, and new legislation. - **TxDMV**: Provides the latest rules on registration, insurance, and driver licensing. - **Texas Legislature**: Bills and statutes can be tracked on the Texas Legislature Online portal. ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they override general rules. 2. **Use hands‑free** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your vehicle’s inspection status** before traveling long distances. 4. **Keep a copy of your insurance card** in the vehicle. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular driving scenario!
